LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 11 picks, including the Jaguars to handle the Giants on the road Imagn Images Stacking winning weeks is always a good feeling when it comes to picking NFL games . I did that the past two weeks. After a good Week 9 picking games, I was solid again in Week 10. I went 9-5 against the spread and 8-6 straight up. I'll take it. Two weeks in a row. Wow. The records after 10 weeks are now 95-54-1 straight up and 68-79-3 ATS. Climbing out of a huge hole, ATS has me now visibly seeing the .500 mark. Let's hope the hot streak stays as we move towards Thanksgiving. There are a ton of big spreads this week, so watch out. The dogs might be barking. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Indianapolis Colts (+12.5) at Houston Texans Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime If the Texans are to have any chance of making the playoffs, they have to win this one. The Colts are pretty much done, but they beat Miami last week. Daniel Jones struggled in that one, but the Texans' defense has really struggled. Look for the Colts to hang around here, but the Texans will win it. Pick: Texans 30, Colts 27 Miami Dolphins (+16.5) at Buffalo Bills Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Miami is playing consecutive road games after losing at Indianapolis, while the Bills are home for the first time after two road games. The Bills are playing better on defense in recent weeks against some lower-level quarterbacks. They get another one here in backup Kyle McCord . The Bills will score, as Josh Allen always plays well against Miami, but Miami stays around. Pick: Bills 31, Dolphins 19 New Orleans Saints (+11.5) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a bye, while the Saints lost to the Panthers last week. Chicago is much improved on defense. With the Saints unable to run the ball, it will put a lot of pressure on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough . Caleb Williams will bounce back from his four-interception game last time out against Tampa Bay and will play well here. Bears take it. Pick: Bears 24, Saints 16 Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) The Cowboys are bad on defense, but the Titans haven't exactly lit it up on offense. Cam Ward has played better as of late. Even so, look for the Cowboys offense to have a big day throwing it against a Tennessee defense that struggles against the pass. Dak Prescott will put up big numbers. Pick: Cowboys 37, Titans 23 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+7) at Detroit Lions The issue here is whether Baker Mayfield will play for the Bucs. If not, they will have big problems. The Lions are back home after beating up the Patriots in Germany last week. The offense was dominant that day, but this Tampa Bay defense is playing well. That will keep them in the game, but the uncertainty at quarterback will be too much to overcome. Pick: Lions 22, Bucs 17 Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs (-16.5) Carson Beck makes his first road start for the Cardinals and this is as tough as any place in the league to do so. The Chiefs are coming off an impressive road victory in which Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes. The defense is third in the league in scoring. That will make for a tough day for this limited Arizona offense. Blowout. Pick: Chiefs 33, Cardinals 14 Pittsburgh Steelers (-4.5) at Philadelphia Eagles The Eagles are coming off a bye, while the Steelers are coming off a loss to division-rival Cincinnati. The Eagles are a shell of the team they were early in the season because of injuries and trades. This battle of Pennsylvania has lost some luster. Look for the Steelers to bounce back with a tough defensive effort against an undermanned offense, and Aaron Rodgers will play well. Pick: Steelers 26, Eagles 13 Baltimore Ravens (+2.5) at Carolina Panthers Both of these teams are in desperation mode when it comes to needing victories for the postseason. The Ravens lost at home Monday night to the previously winless Chargers and now have to head out on the road on a short week. That's tough. The Panthers played better defense last week against the Saints, which will help them here. Carolina wins it late, but it's close. Pick: Panthers 23, Ravens 22 New York Jets at Los Angeles Chargers (-3.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Chargers won for the first time on Monday night, beating the Ravens on the road. They actually showed some offensive life in that game. The Jets have defensive issues, which the Chargers can take advantage of here. Quarterback Geno Smith is banged up for the Jets, which could mean rookie Cade Klubnik makes his first NFL start. Look for the Chargers to take advantage if that is the case as they get to 2-8 behind another solid showing by the offense. Pick: Chargers 28, Jets 24 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Fernando Mendoza will be making his first road start, which can be tough for a rookie. But it's also against a really good defense coming off a bye in a tough place to play. That's a real challenge. Look for the Broncos to get after him in this one. The Raiders ' defense isn't playing well, so maybe it's just what Bo Nix needs. Broncos big. Pick: Broncos 31, Raiders 14 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants This is a big game for both teams. The Jaguars are 7-2 and playing as well as any team in the league. But they are playing consecutive road games against a Giants team pushing for a division title. This game will be decided by the Giants' defense against the Jaguars' offense. I think the Jaguars get the better of it. Look for them to run it well with Bhayshul Tuten . Pick: Jaguars 26, Giants 17 Minnesota Vikings at San Francisco 49ers (-3) In Mexico, Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the best game of the week, featuring two of the NFC's best. The 49ers beat Dallas last week, while the Vikings beat the Packers in Kirk Cousins ' first game back with the team after being traded by the Raiders. This will be about the 49ers offense vs. Brian Flores' defense. I think Kyle Shanahan will get the best of it as the 49ers keep rolling. Big day for Christian McCaffrey running it. Pick: 49ers 23, Vikings 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Washington Commanders (+6.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals are rolling on offense as Joe Burrow pushes toward the MVP. The Commanders have had problems against the pass, ranking 31st in the league, which has to have Burrow and the offense ready to go. Jayden Daniels won't keep up, but it's close. The Bengals keep rolling. Stroud an the Houston Texans need every win they can get to make the playoffs in the AFC, and oddsmakers are expecting them to get one on Thursday night against the Indianapolis Colts. The Texans are heavily favored at home against Daniel Jones and the Colts, who are just 3-7 this season even though they beat the Miami Dolphins in Week 10. Indy traded away a bunch of key pieces at the deadline, but it did knock off Houston earlier in the season. After entering the season as the favorite to win the AFC South, the Texans have lost a bunch of games that they were favored in, going just 2-5 against the spread as a favorite. Houston blew a 17-0 lead against the Cleveland Browns in Week 10 and has losses against Indy, the New York Giants and others that have led it to a 3-6 start. The No. 7 seed in the AFC is still possible for the Texans, but they may need to win out to make it happen with Cleveland (6-4) now holding the head-to-head tiebreaker between the two teams. After opening as 10-point favorites in this matchup with the Colts, the Texans have since shifted to 12.5-point favorites at home. Indy didn't look too impressive against a Miami team starting a rookie quarterback, but should bettors lay the 12.5 points with the Texans? Here's a look at the odds and a take from the SI Betting team on this primetime matchup. Colts vs. Texans Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Colts +12.5 (-102) Texans -12.5 (-118) 44.5 (Over -105/Under -115) Houston's struggles against the spread this season are hard to look past, and the Texans have one impressive win -- against Jacksonville -- in the 2026 season. While the Colts are clearly building for the future after the deadline, this may be a few too many points to give them in this matchup. As a result, SI Betting's Iain MacMillan shared in his Road to 272 column -- where he bets on every game, every week -- why he is targeing the OVER in this matchup: With the spread in the double digits, I have no interest in backing either team. Instead, I'm going to take the OVER. The Texans' offense has been their strength this season. They're now ninth in the league in EPA per play and fourth in that metric since Week 4. C.J. Stroud has also been phenomenal, ranking inside the top eight in almost every quarterback metric since Week 4. Now they'll get to feast against a horrific Colts defense that's 21st in opponent EPA per play. Of course, it's hard to trust the Colts' offense, but it's time for us to continue to assume that the Houston offense is going to turn things around and become the elite unit it was the past few seasons. The biggest red flag in this game is that they're 22nd in opponent rush EPA and 27th in opponent rush success rate, which will feed directly into the Colts' offensive strength with Jonathan Taylor. MacMillan's bet may be the way to go with both of these teams struggling in 2026 and ranking in the bottom half of th league in EPA/Play on defense. It'll be interesting to see if this line moves even further towards the Texans before Thursday night's matchup. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. picks.blurb: Colts vs. Texans Best Anytime Touchdown Scorer Picks for Thursday Night Football in NFL Week 11 Skip to main content BUY THE ISSUE PREDICTION MARKETS Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans may not be known for playing high-scoring games this season, but there's still a way to bet on a few players to find the end zone in this standalone matchup on Thursday night. Week 11 kicks off in Houston with C.J. Stroud and company favored by double digits against Daniel Jones and the tanking Colts, who traded away multiple key players at the deadline. Despite that, the Colts are 3-7 and Houston is just 3-6 entering the second meeting between these teams in the 2026 season. The total in this game is in the mid-40s, which means we should see a few touchdowns on each side, especially with both of these defenses ranking in the bottom half of the league in EPA/Play. On the Houston side, it's going to be the passing game that has to get the job done in this one, as David Montgomery has been banged up with a groin injury and Woody Marks suffered a concussion in Sunday's loss against Cleveland. That leaves Stroud with very few options outside of his receiving corps, where Nico Collins has been the clear No. 1 option. As for the Colts, it's the Jonathan Taylor show with several pieces gone at the deadline. Jones hasn't exactly led the team on a ton of touchdown drives in 2026, so bettors may want to be careful with the number of Colts they’re willing to bet on in this game. I found a few players to target to find the end zone to kick off Thursday night in Week 11. Best Anytime Touchdown Scorer Picks for Colts vs. Texans Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Jonathan Taylor Anytime TD (+110) Taylor was the subject of trade rumors at the deadline, but he remains in Indy and should be the top option in this offense heading into Week 11. Oddsmakers have set plenty of Taylor’s props lower with Seth McGowan getting involved in this backfield in recent weeks, yet Taylor has still played over 67 percent of the offensive plays in all but one game in the 2026-27 season. He hasn't found the end zone since Week 7, so there is some risk when it comes to this bet and the shaky Indy offense. Still, Taylor has eight scores in the 2026 campaign, and is taking on a Houston team that has allowed 12 rushing scores. The Texans’ defense is just 20th in EPA/Rush and is allowing 4.0 yards per carry. Taylor handled 25 touches the last time these two teams met, so I don’t mind as an anytime touchdown scorer pick with this offense devoid of playmakers. Nico Collins Anytime TD (-105) Houston wideout Nico Collins has found the end zone in back-to-back weeks, and he has five touchdowns in seven appearances in the 2026 season. The clear No. 1 option for this Houston offense through the air, Collins has already seen 55 targets from C.J. Stroud, reeling in 37 of them for 478 yards. He was targeted 16 times in the loss to Cleveland in Week 10, and with the Houston running game struggling in 2026, I expect the offense to rely on Stroud throwing the ball on Thursday. The Colts have allowed 17 passing touchdowns this season, but Collins missed the first meeting against them with an injury. I think he makes his presence felt on Thursday night and scores for the third game in a row. Dalton Schultz Anytime TD (+175) Texas tight end Dalton Schultz found the end zone for the first time this season in Week 10, catching one of his two targets for 11 yards and a score. Schultz’s role has diminished with Houston getting healthier at receiver, but he’s still received four or more targets in six of his nine appearances this season. Both of these offenses have some question marks at the skill positions, so I don’t mind trusting a veteran like Schultz who has a clear this season. In Week 3 against Indy, Schultz had three grabs for 30 yards, and the Colts have allowed seven scores to opposing tight ends – the fifth-most in the league. With Houston likely to throw the ball a ton again in Week 11, I don’t mind taking a shot on Schultz since backup tight end Foster Moreau hasn’t been targeted in each of his last three games. away.blurb: The final injury reports are leaking out for both the Houston Texans and Indianapolis Colts, and it's currently looking like Houston will undoubtedly have the medical advantage in a little over 24 hours. All the major injuries from before will keep the same crop of playmakers out on Thursday. However, the Colts are faced with a catastrophe of injuries that will ensure a skeleton crew approach on Amazon Prime. Sauce Gardner, cornerback: calf (projected to be Questionable) Anthony Gould, wide receiver: toe (projected to be Questionable) Charlie Heck, offensive tackle: personal (projected to be Questionable) Will Mallory, tight end: hamstring (projected to be OUT) Bernhard Raimann, offensive tackle: concussion (projected to be OUT) Luke Rhodes, longsnapper: hamstring (projected to be Questionable) Jerry Tillery, defensive tackle: calf (projected to be OUT) Jalen Travis, offensive tackle: knee (projected to be OUT) Charvarius Ward, cornerback: knee (projected to be OUT) On Houston's side, they're dealing with an injury slate the looks like: Kamari Lassiter, cornerback: wrist (reportedly in line to play) Houston Texans have significant injury advantage against the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday Night On the Colts' side of things, things look much bleeker on the personnel front. After conducting a walk-through on Wednesday, their projected injury concerns are: By my count, that's two cornerbacks, one wide receiver, three offensive tackles, one tight end, one defensive tackle and even a longsnapper that have some type of designation before the contest. Thats after already not having the likes of DeForest Buckner, Keenan Allen, Alec Pierce Josh Downs and Quenton Nelson on the team at the moment due to either injury or trade offs at the NFL trade deadline. Getty The Buffalo Bills could rely on a veteran cornerback against the Miami Dolphins. Buffalo is coming off a road win over the New York Jets to improve to 8-1 and is atop the AFC. The Bills have been playing great, but they did suffer some key injuries in the win, which could mean the team has to make some roster moves. Buffalo is set to host the Dolphins on Sunday. Buffalo Bills Predicted to Promote Tre'Davious White GettyBills predicted to promote Tre'Davious White. In the Bills' win over the Jets, starting cornerback Christian Benford suffered an injury, which is a bit of a concern. However, if Benford can't go, Bills reporter Joe Buscagalia of The Athletic believes the team will elevate Tre'Davious White from the practice squad. "Tre'Davious White is on the practice squad, and this is why the Bills brought him back in the first place," Buscagalia wrote . "That's also why they decided against going after another veteran cornerback in the trade market. … "If Benford has to miss any time, the Bills might need White to play as early as next week. And if it goes well enough, maybe even earn a bigger role as the year goes on." White would be entering his 11th NFL season. He signed with Buffalo's practice squad during the year as he wanted to return after starting 16 games and playing well a year ago. Buffalo selected White in the first round of the 2017 NFL Draft, and he became a lockdown corner. Although he's no longer the No. 1 cornerback he once was, he can add some depth to the cornerback room if Benford is out. White Believes He's Ready to Play White has been on the Bills' practice squad and could get his first elevation against the Dolphins on Sunday. The veteran cornerback spoke to The Athletic and admitted he's feeling good and ready to play. "Everybody's been telling me I look good, so there it is. You know, I always leave it to my teammates and my peers," the 31-year-old said. "I always say it like, 'Hey, you see me out there and I look like I'm walking, just tell me to hang it up.' And nobody told me to hang it up yet, Joe, so I'm good, man, I feel like I am good." White, meanwhile, has also been mentoring rookie Davison Igbinosun and sophomore Maxwell Hairston. It's a different role for White, but along with mentoring, he knows he's here to play. "This ain't have to be what it was; this is what I chose," White said. "You know what I mean? I could have been anywhere else on a team, on a 53, playing right now, but I'm a Bill. … I mean, it's bigger than me, man." "I know I can go out there and play right now. Movement good, body feels good, I know how I can play, but right now my role is to help the young guys out and to be that. But it's hard, being that I just started every game last year, you know what I mean? And played good football. So it's like, ' Ahh .' But I'm going to trust the process, and I'm gonna be here to cheer the guys on. But as I'm doing it, I'm definitely preparing to play, too." The Bills are 8-1. The Bills are off to their best start since 1991 after a 31-12 win over the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium in Week 10. Josh Allen ran for two touchdowns and threw another to DJ Moore, while James Cook broke a 74-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter to put the game away. Buffalo is 3-1 at home and leads the race for the AFC's No.1 seed. Meanwhile, the Dolphins have dropped three straight since their lone win over the Jets in Week 7, falling to the Patriots, Lions, and the Colts. That last game came with Kyle McCord making his first NFL start after Malik Willis landed on injured reserve with a core muscle injury. McCord was solid, throwing for 209 yards and running for a score, but a strip-sack returned for a touchdown to open the second half proved costly. Miami has been competitive lately, with four of its last five games decided by eight points or fewer, but overall, they are just 1-4 on the road. Dolphins vs. Bills Kickoff, Weather, TV, Streaming Info Kickoff is Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park, New York. CBS carries the game in the United States. In Canada, the game can be streamed nationwide on DAZN through NFL Game Pass, while CTV and RDS carry selected Sunday afternoon games depending on regional coverage. For Sunday, November 22 at Highmark Stadium, the current forecast is around 16°C at kickoff, with a mix of sun and clouds and south to southwest winds around 13 to 19 km/h. There is still some disagreement on shower chances, but the latest Buffalo-area forecast is mostly dry. NFL Betting Odds, Point Spread, Trends The Bills are 16.5-point favourites with a -1200 money line , tied for the biggest spread on the Week 11 board. The visiting Dolphins are placed at +750 , while the game total sits at 45.5 . Buffalo has been one of the best bets in football this season, going 7-2 against the spread behind the league's top-scoring offence. Allen has been a dual threat, and Cook just shredded the Jets for 157 yards on 18 carries. The one blemish is ball security, as Allen has thrown an interception in four of the Bills' last five games, which gives an opportunistic defence a path to stealing a possession or two. As for the Dolphins, the offence has been held to 22 points or fewer in each of its last three games, and now it's working with a quarterback who had never taken an NFL snap before last week. Miami is 4-5 against the spread and has hung around in most of its losses, but its only other game as a double-digit underdog this season was a 35-13 loss in San Francisco. The defence also just lost defensive tackle Zach Sieler for the season with a ruptured biceps. The over is 5-4 in both teams' games. With the Bills rolling and Miami down its starting quarterback and best interior defender, siding with Buffalo makes sense, though 16.5 points is a massive number in a division game, and the Dolphins' knack for keeping things close makes the backdoor cover a possibility. NFL Player Odds and Props Caleb Douglas OVER 49.5 receiving yards Rookie Caleb Douglas has emerged as Miami's most dangerous receiver. He leads the Dolphins in receiving yards on the season after a six-catch, 70-yard day against Detroit and a two-touchdown breakout game against the Jets earlier in the campaign. As a 16.5-point underdog, Miami is likely to be throwing for much of the second half, and Douglas is the one receiver on this roster who can make plays down the field. Garbage-time volume against a Bills defence protecting a big lead could go a long way. James Cook OVER 74.5 rushing yards James Cook just ran for 157 yards on 18 carries against the Jets and now he gets a Dolphins front that will be without Zach Sieler, its best interior defender, for the rest of the season. As massive home favourites, the Bills should be leaning on the run in the second half to protect a lead, and Cook has shown he can break off a long one at any moment, as his 74-yard touchdown last week proved. McCord, a 2025 sixth-round pick of the Eagles who was acquired from Green Bay in August, completed 17-of-32 passes for 209 yards in his debut and showed enough poise to give Miami a chance late, driving into Colts territory before a sack and a batted pass ended the comeback. Willis will miss at least four games, so this is McCord's offence to run for the foreseeable future. Ollie Gordon II remains the workhorse in the backfield, and Douglas, Malik Washington, and tight end Greg Dulcich round out the passing game. The defence has been opportunistic, with Chris Johnson returning an interception 59 yards for a touchdown last week, but losing Sieler hurts a front that already struggled to get after the quarterback. Jeff Hafley has said the offence has to run the ball well, and against Buffalo, shortening the game with Gordon and forcing Allen into mistakes is Miami's only realistic path to keeping this close. Allen continues to make everything go for the Bills, and the supporting cast is as deep as it's been in years. DJ Moore has become a reliable deep threat, Dalton Kincaid ripped off a 54-yard catch against the Jets to set up a touchdown, and Cook gives Buffalo a home-run hitter out of the backfield. The Bills put up 31 points on the road last week even with a quiet first half, pulling away after halftime with a series of explosive plays. Defensively, Buffalo held the Jets to four field goals and forced turnovers, with linebacker Terrel Bernard delivering the hit that knocked Geno Smith out of the game and rookie cornerback Davison Igbinosun picking off rookie Cade Klubnik. Against a rookie quarterback making just his second start, Joe Brady's defence should be able to dictate the action. away.blurb: The only other player who has now been hit with a DNP (did not participate) is rookie wide receiver Chris Bell. Bell is still dealing with a knee injury, which is connected to his torn ACL that he suffered at the end of his collegiate career in 2025. Bell has appeared on the injury report off and on since returning in Week 1 to play, and now he was downgraded from a limited participant on Wednesday to DNP on Thursday. Long snapper Tucker Addington (shoulder), cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. (knee ), edge Malik Herring (neck), tight end Will Kacmarek (quad/knee), and wide receiver Jared Wayne (quad) were all limited. away.headline: Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More
away.blurb: The issue at wide receiver is that rookie Caleb Douglas joined the list of injured players at that position as he was limited with a shoulder injury. There was good news there, though, with Chris Bell back at practice (albeit on a limited basis) after both he and Jared Wayne missed the game against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Along with the five players who didn't practice, the Dolphins had five others who were limited. Besides Bell and Douglas, there was LS Tucker Addington again (shoulder), CB JuJu Brents (neck) and C Andrew Meyer (neck). The Bills also had five players sit out practice Wednesday, with guard O'Cyrus Torrence's absence related to a personal issue. Furthermore, three safeties were limited in practice, including recent acquisition Amani Hooker (knee) along with Damar Hamlin (toe) and Cole Bishop (shoulder). Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More Skip to main content SI.COM Center Aaron Brewer missing another practice as he remains in the concussion protocol clearly was the biggest headline of the Miami Dolphins' first injury report for Week 11, but there are several other issues worth monitoring. The most glaring ones would be at wide receiver, where injuries continue to happen, and at punter. The situation with punter Bradley Pinion missing practice because a right groin injury maybe shouldn't have been easy to predict after the Dolphins signed punter Jack Browning to the practice squad earlier Wednesday. As a general rule, NFL teams don't have two punters or two kickers on the team (active roster and practice squad) unless there's an injury, so the Browning move should have been a sign. As we indicated earlier, Browning has appeared in five NFL games but none since the 2024 season and hasn't even punted in a preseason since then. Wayne was among the five players who didn't practice, a group that included safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin) and cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee). Trader has been battling injuries for a few weeks now and one wonders whether he'll need to be shut down at some point to allow him to get back to 100 percent. While it's early in the week, the best projection if Trader can't play against Buffalo would be for Zayne Anderson to get the start alongside rookie Michael Taaffe even if Kyle Louis has been getting regular snaps on defense since coming off IR. Louis has been used as a type of nickel linebacker as opposed to a true safety. Simpson is primarily a special teams contributor, and if Wayne can't play again, then it would mean another game for veteran Jalen Tolbert. In the event that both Brewer and Meyer wound up sidelined for the Buffalo game, then we'd be looking at Jarrett Kingston, who played center for two snaps against the Colts when Meyer briefly left the game. The focus for Buffalo should be in the secondary, which was missing Wednesday cornerbacks Dee Alford (concussion) and Christian Benford (groin). Published 1 minute ago ALAIN POUPART Ala

home.blurb: White Ready to Return to Action Reports indicate the Bills will elevate White from the practice squad if Benford cannot go. Joe Buscgalia of The Athletic wrote that the team planned for this exact moment. "Tre'Davious White is on the practice squad, and this is why the Bills brought him back in the first place," Buscaglia wrote. White is entering his 11th NFL season and knows the system well. He signed with Buffalo earlier this year specifically to return to the lineup. The veteran cornerback told reporters he feels strong and ready to help. White has been clear about his mindset regarding his age and role. He told The Athletic, "Everybody's been telling me I look good, so there it is. "I always say it like, 'Hey, you see me out there and I look like I'm walking, just tell me to hang it up.' And nobody told me to hang it up yet, Joe, so I'm good, man, I feel like I am good." away.blurb: Panthers vs. Saints injury report: Is Jaelan Phillips making return? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Panthers vs. Saints injury report: Is Jaelan Phillips making return? The Carolina Panthers are in a divisional battle this week as they're set to face the New Orleans Saints. Ahead of the matchup, the status of Jaelan Phillips was in question as he's dealt with a hamstring injury for several weeks. The good news is that it looks like he'll be making his return to the field, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. "Panthers edge Jaelan Phillips, who has been out since mid-October with a hamstring injury, is expected to play today, source said. He's listed as questionable," Rapoport wrote on X, formerly Twitter. Phillips is listed as questionable against the Saints, but it looks like he'll be playing. He was a full participant in practice during the middle of the week, but was then limited the next day. That may have raised some concern for some, but the good news is that he'll be back on the field. With the return of Phillips, they should have a good chance of getting back on track, and it'll be an interesting matchup against the Saints, who also have three wins this season and are in second place in the division. Malik Brown, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Sun, November 15, 2026 at 3:44 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Jaelan Phillips' injury status vs. Saints Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Panthers definitely need Phillips' production, as their defense hasn't been the best this season. One of the reasons is injuries, and they're slowly getting back healthy. They've lost their last three games, but the funny thing is that they're still leading the division with a 3-5 record. It's once again been a slugfest in the NFC South, and there's a chance that the winner of the division won't have to win more than eight games. The Panthers did it last season by winning eight games, and they'll be looking to make it a second year in a row as the division champs. home.headline: Bears get great news on Luther Burden III, Kyle Monangai ahead of Week 11
home.blurb: The Chicago Bears are coming out of their Week 10 bye with a 7-2 record, looking to keep pace with the Minnesota Vikings and Detroit Lions atop the division. It's not going to be easy, especially now that the Vikings have Kirk Cousins. But, fortunately for the Bears, they got some great news coming out of their Week 10 bye. Both might still be questionable, but Burden and Monangai look to be on track to suit up coming out of the bye. If that's the case, this offense might finally be fully healthy. home.headline: Chicago Bears: Jeffery Simmons pops up with surprise injury
home.blurb: On Wednesday’s injury report, Simmons was estimated as a limited participant in practice due to a knee injury. Cornerback Kyler Gordon was estimated as a non-participant due to a shoulder injury. Luther Burden III, Kyle Monangai and Malik Muhammad were estimated as full participants. DK Metcalf called out for alarming habit during games The Chicago Bears have put two quarterbacks on the injury report ever since they traded for Jeffery Simmons, but the defensive tackle is dealing with an injury coming off the bye in Week 10. The Bears harassed Sam Darnold in their win over the Seattle Seahawks in Week 8, causing the quarterback to miss two games due to a rib injury. Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is trending toward not playing the Detroit Lions this week after the Week 10 bye due to a foot/ankle injury he suffered in Week 9. While Simmons and the Bears defensive line have been getting after the quarterback, the star defensive tackle has sustained some damage. Jeffery Simmons as Chicago Bears thinking Super Bowl Simmons didn’t speculate about the injury during his appearance on “The Rich Eisen Show” last week. Based on the injury report, the issue appears to be minor, but there could be a concern before the Bears host the New Orleans Saints on Sunday. When talking to Eisen last week, Simmons was more worried about the big picture, gaining confidence one game at a time while they make a run for the Super Bowl. “For me it’s one day at a time, one game at a time,” Simmons said . “I really think everything will take care of itself. We have a really great team. It takes all three phases, and if we can stay healthy, the sky is the limit for this team. “When I walk into the building, when I walk into the meeting rooms, you can feel what Coach Ben (Johnson) is preaching and trying to build in Chicago. The confidence that they have in that building, it was there before I got there. You see it all over social media in the locker room after the game, and that brings confidence to your guys.” The Bears are certainly more confident with Simmons on the field. Between deadline trades that added strength to the franchise's rebuild and promising development from young players across the board, the Robert Saleh era is slowly building into something fans can get behind. In Week 11, his Titans team has a chance to win their second game of the season on the road vs. the Dallas Cowboys. Here's one reason they'll get it done, one reason they'll fall short, and my own prediction for how things will ultimately pan out. Will: Cam Ward, Tony Pollard have big games The Cowboys, after allowing 46 points to the San Francisco 49ers in a loss last week, just turned over defensive play-calling duties to senior assistant coach Mike Pettine. Dallas' defense is struggling, and if the Titans win, it'll be because Cam Ward and Tony Pollard take advantage of that. Ward has been on a short tear as of late, doubling his touchdown total through seven games in the last two. The second-season QB has also eclipsed 200 yards in back-to-back games for the first time this year. With WR Carnell Tate likely to return, Ward is tracking for another leap. On the ground, meanwhile, the Cowboys' rushing defense is last in the league in yards allowed per game (154.1) and yards per carry (5.2). This marks Pollard's first game against his former team; the numbers are supportive, and the stakes are there. The Titans' offense has simply been on a team-wide heater as of late. It'll take another inspired performance from key playmakers to pull it off, but Tennessee has a clear angle to a road win. Won't: Titans' defense continues downward spiral However, Tennessee's defense has been trending in the opposite direction. As has been the case in the past two weeks, Saleh's bunch have mostly erased positive offensive momentum and cost the Titans' two chances at winnable games. If Tennessee were to fall short in Week 11, I have to think it would be for the same reason. The Titans' previous two opponents have crossed the 40 mark, and Dallas, in spite of their loss, score as much against a better 49ers defense this past week. As Saleh himself said after the team's latest loss, you aren't going to win allowing 40 points a game. The Titans' previous two opponents have crossed the 40 mark, and Dallas, in spite of their loss, score as much against a better 49ers defense this past week. Dallas is a veteran-led group in the middle of a difficult year; their down season can't be compared to that of the Titans, and QB Dak Prescott is sure to run this defense through the ringer. On the road after arguably their worst showing of the year, Saleh's defense has their back against the wall. Prediction: Titans win, 30-27 With that said, I still think the Titans find a way to pull this one out. If the away team can strike a balance between their growing offensive attack and a defense that isn't allowing Dallas to do whatever they want, a close win is in the cards. The Titans have yet to play a full, complete game this year. Even their Week 6 victory over the Indianapolis Colts saw Tennessee trailing 13-0 at halftime. I'm predicting that the Titans get this done, and do so by offering a solid showing through all four quarters. That means a consistent Cam Ward, a defense that bends, but doesn't break, reliable play-calling on either side of the ball, and at least a little good luck on the injury front. A lot has to go right, but this game wouldn't have been seen as winnable only a few short weeks ago. For that reason, I believe the Titans will win it. away.blurb: The premise remains hypothetical, and there are still eight weeks left in the regular season. But Rowland’s standard is clear if Tennessee remains in the top slot: It should not move off Smith for an ordinary trade package. It should demand a return large enough to reshape the roster. The Tennessee Titans enter Week 11 at 1-8 and occupy the No. 1 spot in the 2027 NFL Draft order, creating a hypothetical that could define the club’s offseason. If the order holds, Locked On Titans host Tyler Rowland believes Tennessee should try to get a historic haul rather than taking Ohio State junior wide receiver Jeremiah Smith. Rowland’s position is not that Smith lacks the talent to warrant being the first overall pick. He called Smith a “generational freak prospect” and argued that a modest move down the board would not justify passing on him. Rowland’s asking price is much higher: three first-round picks, preferably including several selections near the top of the draft. “I am taking the three first-round picks,” Rowland said. He framed the choice around roster construction, arguing that one elite non-quarterback cannot fill enough holes for a rebuilding Tennessee roster. In his preferred version of a trade, the Titans would use the extra picks to add several premium prospects. That argument has more weight because Tennessee already owns the Chicago Bears’ 2027 first-round pick and 2028 first-round pick after its October trade of defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. Another major trade package would give the Titans unusual freedom to address several areas of the roster around quarterback Cam Ward rather than relying on one draft choice to change the offense. Rowland made one exception to his rule: a quarterback prospect he considers truly rare. He said he would decline an offer of three first-round picks for that type of passer, but he does not view a non-quarterback, even one with Smith’s profile, as untouchable at that price. away.headline: Tennessee Titans add WR Jamari Thrash to practice squad
away.blurb: With Restrepo moving to the active roster, the Titans had an open spot on the practice squad and wasted little time in signing wide receiver Jamari Thrash, who worked out with the Titans on November 9, to replace Restrepo on the practice squad. The 5-foot-11, 188-pound wideout entered the league as a fifth-round pick by the Cleveland Browns in the 2024 NFL Draft, made the roster out of training camp, and saw action in nine games as a rookie. He followed that up with another nine games in 2025, finishing his Browns career with 13 receptions for 129 yards. The Tennessee Titans made a small roster move on Tuesday, placing wide receiver Wan’Dale Robinson on injured reserve and then signing fan-favorite Xavier Restrepo to the active 53-man roster. This move should open reps for both Restrepo and Chimere Dike in the slot, and help Cam Ward and the Titans’ offense attack the middle of the field. Thrash was injured during training camp in 2026 and was eventually waived in September as part of an injury settlement. He would spend time with the Las Vegas Raiders ’ practice squad before being released at the end of October. Thrash should join his new teammates when they take to the field on Wednesday to start preparations for their Week 11 matchup with the Dallas Cowboys. RB Bucky Irving has tallied 825 rushing yards and seven touchdowns this season, and he has carried the ball 71 times over Tampa's last three games. He has cashed the Over on his carries total in 12 of his last 15 games. Irving's total carries sit at 16.5 ( -110 both ways) , and I absolutely love the Over, as they should rely on him early and often with a rookie QB. The Bucs have the most rushing yards per game (163.9), and they set a franchise record with 324 rushing yards earlier this season when they beat the Falcons 16-0; they didn't attempt a single pass in that game. Understandably, they rank dead last in the NFL in passing yards per game (141.9). This Buccaneers offence isn't elite by any means, but their defence is one of the league's best units. Tampa Bay allows 19.8 PPG (sixth in the NFL), and they lead the league in takeaways (21). The Lions offence should be feared. They're scoring 28.6 PPG (sixth in the NFL), and they have the third-most yards per game in the league (392.4). Although the offence often gets most of the glamour, the defence has quietly held four straight opponents to 21 points or fewer, and Detroit is 6-0 when it forces a turnover. These stats matter when they're facing a rookie QB. Detroit's biggest issue is their injury report. Getting Brian Branch back last week from his Achilles tear was a big boost to the secondary, but All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell is on IR (neck), Hutchinson is out for the season, and Kerby Joseph (knee), D.J. Reed (hip), and Cade Mays (ankle) did not travel to Germany last week. Bucs vs. Lions Week 11 Score Prediction Drake Maye exiting the Germany game early didn't help my Over last week, and if I learned anything with that loss it was to not count on an offence without their starting QB. Tampa's defence can keep this game close, but expect a low-scoring affair. I'll bet the Under and tune into a few of Sunday's other games featuring more offensive star power. Hutchinson, who has six sacks this season, eventually walked off the field under his own power. He entered the blue medical tent on the sideline and remained there for a few moments before later walking to the locker room with trainers at his side. Campbell is scheduled to hold a news conference on Tuesday. If the report from NFL Network is correct and Hutchinson does have a torn ACL, D.J. Wonnum and rookie Derrick Moore would be expected to see an uptick in responsibilities. Wonnum has six sacks this season, and Moore has four over his last two games.

away.headline: The Chiefs face a rare in-season opportunity with the Cardinals coming to KC
away.blurb: The Cardinals are without their leading wide receiver, Michael Wilson, who injured his back earlier this month and is out for the season. And first-round pick Jeremiyah Love, the running back, is on injured reserve because of an ankle issue. The Chiefs are 16- to 16.5-point favorites against the Cardinals on Sunday. Arizona has lost its last two games by a combined score of 51-9. The Chiefs may rest injured players before playing the Bills on Thanksgiving. You don’t have to be a soothsayer to know that Chiefs coach Andy Reid will be looking forward to the challenge of playing the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday at Arrowhead Stadium. It’s what Reid says each week about the Chiefs’ next opponent. The oddsmakers aren’t so sure it’ll be a challenge for the Chiefs. BetMGM has the Chiefs as a 16-point favorite , while DraftKings has the line at 16 1/2 points . It’s rare to see a team be favored by more than two scores, but that’s where things stand. And it makes for an interesting and rare NFL opportunity facing the Chiefs: Should they rest players Sunday because of a short turnaround into their next game? After playing the Cardinals, the Chiefs will take on the AFC-leading Bills in Buffalo on Thanksgiving. The Chiefs will never publicly say they are pondering resting players given the strength of their opponent, but the Cardinals, 3-7, are down on their luck. After picking up road wins against the Chargers, Rams and Cowboys through the first eight weeks of the season, Arizona has lost its last two games by a combined score of 51-9. Ahead of the NFL trade deadline, the Cardinals dealt their top quarterback (Jacoby Brissett) and wide receiver (Marvin Harrison Jr.). There were 15 players listed on the Cardinals’ injury report last week ahead of Arizona’s game against the Los Angeles Rams. That includes safety Andrew Wingard, who is not expected to play against the Chiefs, according to the team’s website. Four offensive linemen were on that injured list, including Hjalte Froholdt and Jon Gaines II. In the Cardinals’ 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday, linebacker Jordan Burch suffered a season-ending knee injury. Rookie Carson Beck will start at quarterback for the Cardinals because backup Gardner Minshew suffered a season-ending injury. Beck has attempted 18 career NFL passes, and his backups are 40-year-old Josh Johnson and rookie Joey Aguilar. The Cardinals will enter Sunday’s game with the 29th-ranked scoring offense and 31st-ranked scoring defense. The Chiefs also have injuries, and a number of players were hurt during Sunday’s game against the Falcons: guard Trey Smith (concussion), tight end Jared Wiley (broken ankle) and Travis Kelce (calf). Also, rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane landed hard on his back. And the Chiefs played without running back Kenneth Walker, who has a groin injury. Regardless of what the oddsmakers say, no game is a gimme, but the Chiefs might have enough firepower against a short-handed Cardinals team that they could let Walker rest.

home.headline: Kansas City Chiefs HC Andy Reid's injury update after Week 10's win over Falcons spells bad news for 2024 NFL Draft pick
home.blurb: Wiley was carted to the locker room during the first quarter of the blowout win over the Falcons. The team dealt with a few more injuries as the game went on. Reid confirmed that Creed Humphrey got poked in the eye, which was clear on TV. He finished the game and will ultimately be ok. As for CB Mansoor Delane, it seems like he was pulled more so out of an abundance of caution. "He landed on his back and kind of up on that shoulder area," Reid said. "I think he was scared more than anything. He's going to be alright, though." Another injury setback for Delane's shoulder would be troubling, but he sounds like he avoided anything serious. As for Wiley, this is the type of injury that could prematurely end his Chiefs career. As a rookie out of TCU in 2024, Wiley suffered a season-ending ACL injury during practice. That injury really took away the remainder of his rookie season and limited him during the 2025 NFL season as well. It wasn't until this offseason that he felt like he was getting back to himself. However, that never really came to fruition in on-field production. Now, with the ankle fracture that will almost certainly end his season, Wiley is heading for another long rehab and recovery. A fourth-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft out of TCU, Wiley is listed at 6-foot-6 and 250 pounds. The Chiefs have appeared in 50 combined regular-season and postseason games since the start of the 2024 NFL season. Whether it has been injury or a healthy scratch, Wiley has played in 15 of 50 possible games during that timeframe. Wiley is likely slated for IR with the fractured ankle, with eight more games left in the 2026 NFL regular season. As for how the team will adapt to Wiley's loss, it likely opens a needed roster spot, with Omarr Norman-Lott slated to return soon . Kansas City has three tight ends on the 53-man roster currently, with Travis Kelce, Noah Gray, and Jake Briningstool. They have one tight end on the practice squad in the International Player Pathway Program, Thomas Odukoya. picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Giannis red hot vs. Bucks Boone's trade charts Cowboys DC latest Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 17, 2026 at 6:24 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers are hurting in the pride department. Meanwhile, the Philadelphia Eagles are just trying to find their way out of a losing streak. Here are bold predictions as these rivals meet in NFL Week 11. It's weird to write off the Steelers. They have a record of 6-3 and are strongly favored to improve to 7-3 against the weak Eagles. It seems like forever since the Eagles won a game. They beat the Commanders and Titans in tight wins to open the 2026 season before embarking on their current seven-game losing streak. Let's look at what to expect as these teams meet. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers will throw for 225-plus yards with two TDs The Steelers need to re-establish their passing game. They could handle the Eagles by just pounding them on the ground. But this is an opportunity to restore confidence in the passing attack. Rodgers is coming off games with 172 and 143 passing yards. The latter came in an absolute beatdown at the hands of the Bengals. The Steelers need to have good things happen through the air. Rodgers seemed to call out receiver DK Metcalf after the Bengals debacle, according to a post on X by Andrew Fillipponi. "They had a nice plan for some of the run stuff, but they played press coverage, they played a lot of man coverage, and we didn't make them pay at all," Rodgers said after the game. Nobody is going to confuse the 2026 Rodgers with the one who dominated in the past. However, he played well enough for the Steelers to get to 6-2 before the Bengals game. There's reason to believe he can keep this team ahead of the pack when the opponent isn't overwhelming. The Steelers have no chance in the postseason, but they can get there with six more winnable games left on the schedule: Eagles, Texans, Ravens (twice), Panthers, and Titans. Of course, the Steelers will have to make up for the loss of guard Mason McCormick, who suffered a gruesome ankle injury on Sunday night. Head coach Mike McCarthy said there's a plan, according to the Steelers' YouTube page via Yahoo. "Spencer's, you know, he's just a 360 football player, in my view," McCarthy said. "You know, he started out in his right guard and then also the ability to play left guard. He's a gifted football player. This will be his opportunity." Steelers WR DK Metcalf will get 90-plus yards receiving Metcalf has only topped this mark twice this year. He had 115 yards against the Browns and 93 in an overtime game against the Buccaneers. But this is a spot where he could shine again. The Eagles have been middle of the pack against the pass, but they're trending way down overall as a team. There's a good reason for the Steelers to get Metcalf more involved. It not only matters for Rodgers and the team, but the organization has to deal with his five-year, $150 million contract. Oops. If they don't get Metcalf rolling, they may have to look at trying to get out of his contract. That could prove difficult , according to Sports Illustrated. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a pre-June 1 designation next offseason would make minimal sense, as doing so would incur a dead money hit of $35.775 million while only opening up $2.650 million in cap space for the 2027 campaign (per Over the Cap)," Jack Markowski wrote. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a post-June 1 designation in 2027 would save $26.5 million against the cap, however, while also forcing the Steelers to take on $11.925 million in dead money." That's just a lot of ugly numbers. Instead, the Steelers are better off trying to feed Metcalf and see if they can restore the roar he had earlier in his career. Eagles QB Joe Milton will throw for 200-plus yards The Eagles need to see what they have in the young quarterback. He completed only 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards against the Giants. But he also rushed nine times for 64 yards. There's something to like about Milton, but he needs to show better accuracy during this audition that could last for the remainder of the season. Milton reviewed his own performance against the Giants, according to philadelphiaeagles.com. "For my first game here, I feel like I did all right," Milton said. "There are a lot of things that I can clean up as far as protection, just helping those guys out with protection. That's something that we're going to get better (at) this week coming up for sure. "I felt blessed, more blessed. That's about it. I felt more blessed than anything. I was able to see my family in the stands, so it was great, but it was also just great to be out there with the guys that I've been here training with for the past three weeks and learning. And just that communication and connection that the team has, and just being a part of it. I love it. It's great. I wouldn't ask for no better situation than this." It won't be easy against the Steelers' tough defense. But look for Milton to battle through for a good game. That's especially true if he can make a big play early. Confidence is an important part of the equation for a young QB. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) head to Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday for a game against their instate rival, the Philadelphia Eagles (2-7). Although on the road, this game comes at a critical point in the Steelers’ season. With games the next three weeks against the Broncos, the Texans, and the Jaguars - all teams contending for a playoff spot in the AFC - this one is a near must-win against the Birds. Second in the AFC North and sixth in the AFC overall, Aaron Rodgers and co. are a half-game ahead of the Browns and 1.5 games ahead of the Patriots in the postseason chase. The Eagles have struggled for most of the season. Jalen Hurts led Philly to wins in their first two games, but the Eagles have since lost every game as well as their quarterback (blood clots). This season, the Steelers have leaned on Rodgers, a productive running game and a defense that ranks among the league leaders in sacks and turnover differential. The veteran signal-caller has thrown for 2,014 yards with 15 touchdowns and six interceptions, while Jaylen Warren has rushed for 719 yards. Philadelphia’s season has unraveled in large part because of injuries, most notably the aforementioned loss of Hurts to injured reserve with blood clots. That leaves Joe Milton III directing an Eagles offense averaging just 16.4 points and an NFL-low 260.2 yards per game. Pittsburgh’s four-game winning streak came to an abrupt end last Sunday in a 38-18 road loss to Cincinnati. The Bengals completely suffocated the Steelers with Pittsburgh managing only 23 total yards through the first three quarters before producing some offense and points after the game was out of reach. DK Metcalf was held without a catch through three quarters before finishing with two receptions for 54 yards and a touchdown, while the defense spent far too much time on the field. Philadelphia, meanwhile, comes into Sunday’s game rested after its bye but desperately searching for an answer to a disastrous stretch. The Eagles’ most recent game was a 19-11 home loss to the Giants on Nov. 8. Milton made his first Eagles start and completed 18 of 34 passes for just 169 yards. It has been a weekly headline for Philadelphia: “Eagles’ are Offensive on Offense”. The bye, though, may help an injury-ravaged roster: receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) could return after missing the Giants game. Smith’s availability is especially significant because the Eagles badly need another proven weapon alongside Saquon Barkley to make life easier for Milton against a Pittsburgh defense featuring T.J. Watt and one of the NFL’s better pass rushes. Beyond Pittsburgh’s attempt to rebound and Philadelphia’s effort to stop its seven-game skid, the matchup carries a fascinating piece of Pennsylvania rivalry history. The Eagles lead the all-time series 50-29-3, and Pittsburgh has endured an extraordinary drought in Philadelphia. The Steelers have not won in Philly since 1965. They have lost their last 11 games against the Eagles in the City of Brotherly Love. Philadelphia has also dominated the two most recent meetings, winning 27-13 in Philadelphia on Dec. 15, 2024, after a 35-13 home victory in 2022; Pittsburgh’s last win in the series was a 38-29 victory at Heinz Field in 2020. picks.headline: 2026 Steelers Preview: Week 11 vs. the Philadelphia Eagles
picks.blurb: Login/Register Home The 2026 NFL regular season is in full swing, and it's time to preview the Pittsburgh Steelers schedule ahead of every game this season. I'm going to revisit my offseason breakdown of every game on the Steelers schedule as a preview for the upcoming game. I'll be updating the odds and quarterbacks expected to play in the contest, and will only list my offseason prediction. My in-season prediction always comes both on the Steelers Preview podcast Thursday night, as well as on my Friday “Let's Ride” podcast. Here is the detailed breakdown of the Steelers 2026 regular season, continuing with an AFC vs. NFC game vs. the Eagles in Philadelphia. Week 11 at the Philadelphia Eagles Date: Sunday, November 22nd – 1:00pm EST Betting Line: Early Line: Eagles (-5.5) / Total: 42.5 Current Line: Steelers (-4.5) / Total: 38.5 Last Meeting: 12/15/24 – Eagles 27, Steelers 13 Overall Series Record: Philadelphia Eagles lead series 50-29-3 2026 Records: Steelers: 6-3 Projected Starting QB Matchup: Aaron Rodgers vs. Joe Milton or Tanner McKee Analysis: I wanted to convince myself that the Steelers would be able to go into Philadelphia and slay their proverbial dragon. After all, they haven't won in Philadelphia since the Lyndon B. Johnson administration. However, even my optimistic brain can't see a path for them to win the game on the other side of the state. Barring injury, the Eagles defense is going to be a top-notch team in 2026, and while the loss of AJ Brown hurts the offense, they will still have plenty of play makers at their disposal, mainly with a healthy Saquon Barkley. To put it in simple terms, the Eagles are a team the Steelers just don't match up well against. Could they shock the world and break the horrible streak of losing in Philadelphia? I guess anything is possible, but I can't say I am predicting that to take place. I've always said if you could hand pick a loss on the schedule, losing to an NFC opponent on the road would be the choice you should make. And that's exactly what I am predicting in this Week 11 game. Does this loss derail the entire season? I don't think so, but it certainly is a bump in the road. The Steelers will have to dust themselves off quickly as they return to Pittsburgh for a Black Friday game at home vs. the Denver Broncos coming up in Week 12. Prediction: Eagles 26, Steelers 20 Clearly things change from the offseason and schedule release to the upcoming game, but no one saw the collapse of the Eagles in the preseason. How could anyone predict Jalen Hurts being put on Injured Reserve (IR) for blood clots and All-Pro offensive tackle Lane Johnson retiring. I may have thought the Eagles would take a step back, but 2-7 at their bye week was not in my mind. While most would assume the Steelers should dominate the lesser than Eagles, especially after their trade activity, I'm not about to think this game will be easy. I find it difficult to even believe the decades long slump in Philadelphia will end. The Steelers are coming off a drubbing, and the Eagles are coming off their bye week. I think the Steelers win this game, but I don't think I'll spot the 4.5-points. It will be close. It's early, but what are your thoughts on this upcoming game? Will it go as planned? Or will the Eagles continue their dominance over the Steelers in Philly? Let us know your thoughts in the comment section, and be sure to stay tuned to SCN for the latest news and notes on the Steelers as they press on throughout the 2026 regular season. away.headline: Is Pat Freiermuth Playing Tonight? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Steelers vs. Bengals in NFL Week 10)
away.blurb: Pittsburgh Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth was a late addition to the team's injury report on Saturday, as he's now listed as questionable with an illness. We have added TE Pat Freiermuth (illness) to the injury report and he is questionable for Sunday night’s game against Cincinnati. With Freiermuth questionable, I'm targeting the Steelers running game for my favorite prop on Sunday night. Is Pat Freiermuth Playing Tonight? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Steelers vs. Bengals in NFL Week 10) Skip to main content BUY THE ISSUE A late add to the injury report is almost never a good sign, but the fact that Freiermuth is dealing with an illness and didn't suffer an injury is a positive sign for his chances of playing in Week 10. The Steelers have a massive matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals with first place in the AFC North on the line. Freiermuth is part of a key duo at tight end for the Steelers along with Darnell Washington. A former second-round pick, Freiermuth has played in 65.5 percent of the Steelers' snaps this season, catching 25 of his 35 targets for 235 yards and four scores. He's been one of Aaron Rodgers' favorite red-zone targets, but Freiermuth only has one game all season with more than five targets. So, he's a bit of a risky play in the prop makret -- if he's able to suit up on Sunday night. The Steelers have to officially release their inactive list before 7 p.m. EST on Sunday night, so they'll have until then to decide if Freiermuth can play through this illness. Best Steelers Prop Bet vs. Bengals in NFL Week 10 Jaylen Warren OVER 64.5 Rushing Yards (-113) Steelers running back Jaylen Warren is having a monster 2026 season, averaging 5.9 yards per carry while posting four 100-yard games. He’s also cleared 64.5 rushing yards in five of his last six appearances. After entering the season in a timeshare with Rico Dowdle, Warren appears to have taken control of the lead role, playing 72.4 percent of the Steelers’ snaps. A Dowdle injury certainly helped, but Warren has made the most of his opportunities. Cincy ranks 27th in the NFL in EPA/Rush and is allowing a league-high 5.0 yards per carry. Warren torched the Bengals back in Week 3, carrying the ball 17 times for 127 yards while also adding three receptions for 49 yards. He should have another big game on the ground on Sunday night. away.blurb: Head Coach Nick Sirianni expressed optimism during his Wednesday press conference about the possible return of wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) this Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Both players returned to practice coming out of the bye week as they were limited participants on Wednesday. Running back Saquon Barkley, who has played through hamstring and back injuries, was a full participant on Wednesday. He is no longer listed as having a back injury. Fellow running back Will Shipley is on Injured Reserve with a foot injury, but returned to practice on Wednesday as a limited participant. Shipley has been sidelined since the Week 5 game in London. Defensively, linebacker Zack Baun suffered a back injury against the Giants before the bye week and did not practice on Wednesday. He was the only Eagle on the active roster who did not participate in some capacity. Good news is that linebacker Jihaad Campbell is set to return to the lineup after missing two games with hamstring and quad injuries. Wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks are out for Sunday's game, while Giants running back Cam Skattebo is doubtful to play. Dallas Goedert is good to go for Monday, while Saquon Barkley and Jalyx Hunt inch closer to a potential return. TE Dallas Goedert and LB Zack Baun are set to return to action on Sunday. Quarterback Tyson Bagent has cleared concussion protocol and is available for Monday night's game. Who will start at quarterback for the Bears? The Eagles ruled out six players ahead of Sunday's regular-season finale. away.headline: Pittsburgh Steelers cut ties with former Giants wide receiver
away.blurb: The Pittsburgh Steelers have cut ties with wide receiver Isaiah Hodgins , who was on the practice squad with the team since Week 2. Hodgins was added when Max Hurleman went down with a hamstring injury, but with Hurleman’s return, the team has decided to move on. A sixth-round pick out of Oregon State by the Buffalo Bills, Hodgins has experience playing outside and in the slot with the teams. He has 70 receptions for 749 receiving yards and eight touchdowns in his career. Hurleman along with Brandon Johnson still remain on the Steelers’ practice squad. The Steelers have seen Hurleman earn some praise over the last week with Aaron Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy giving him notable praise. Hodgins never was elevated from the practice squad, unlike Johnson and Brandon Smith. Smith remains on the 53-man roster. But the Panthers got back into the win column with a clutch 20-17 victory on the road against the New Orleans Saints. That exorcised some Superdome demons and kept the Panthers in first place in the NFC South for the time being. The Panthers would love to keep stacking wins. They want to win the division first and foremost, but they also want to prove they're a good team regardless, and ending with the franchise's first winning record since 2017 would be excellent. Can they get back to .500 against the Baltimore Ravens this week? Nevertheless, it is good to be favored in a given game, especially a home tilt. The Baltimore Ravens are not the usual Ravens. Lamar Jackson is out, and they've stumbled to a subpar record after facing the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football. That fact, as well as the slightly short week and road trip, may be why the Panthers are favored. Carolina is -130 to win outright ( DraftKings ). Baltimore is +110 on the moneyline. away.headline: NFL fans react to Ravens’ rumored plan for Lamar Jackson’s return after thumb injury
away.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens believe Lamar Jackson has a chance to return from his broken right thumb for their Week 16 game against the Cleveland Browns on Dec. 27 if his rehab goes smoothly, ESPN’s Dan Graziano reported this week. Lamar Jackson’s Road From Buffalo Toward a Possible Browns Return In a statement the team released that day, head coach Jesse Minter called recovery timelines “challenging to predict” and said, “He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return.” Minter added, “We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season.” Graziano’s report hinges on Jackson’s progress in the same way, leaving the Browns game at M&T Bank Stadium a possibility rather than a set date for his return. For another fan, the calendar is the problem, since a return against the Browns would leave Jackson only two more regular-season games after that one. A Dec. 27 return would be near the optimistic end of Jackson’s reported recovery timetable, though the Ravens have emphasized that his progress, rather than a fixed date, will determine when he can play again. The report comes with Baltimore at 4-6, days after a 23-20 home loss to the Los Angeles Chargers, who had not won a game before Monday night. Despite the prospect of Jackson returning for the final stretch of the regular season, several fans who responded to the report argued that the Ravens should keep him sidelined and focus on having him healthy for 2027. Jackson’s injury came on Baltimore’s first offensive play of the Nov. 1 game at Buffalo, a 36-10 loss, when his throwing hand caught the arm of Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau as he threw. On Nov. 13, the Ravens said the thumb was dislocated and broken and that the injury typically carries a recovery of six to 10 weeks. Sources told ESPN’s Adam Schefter that Jackson had undergone surgery the week before. Fans Point to the Baltimore Ravens’ Slide and Jackson’s Long-Term Health “Week 16 is so late. Just shut him down and run it back next year,” the fan wrote. Baltimore’s form has added to the argument. The Ravens sit fourth in the AFC North and have lost five straight games, including the Buffalo game in which Jackson was hurt and both games since. Jacoby Brissett, whom Baltimore acquired in a trade, started in Jackson’s place in the loss to the Chargers. “It’s already over … just take the rest of the season off,” another fan responded. Jackson’s health is another piece of it. A high ankle sprain had already cost him three games before the thumb injury, and he has played just 14 full quarters this season. A fan pointed to that history: “Yea bro let’s have Lamar play meaningless games in a lost season after 2 major injuries.” Others looked straight ahead to next season. “What’s the point to play him at that point, come back ’27 stronger,” one fan wrote. away.headline: NFL Great Trashes Ravens for Making Derrick Henry Change
away.blurb: That drab performance prompted a tirade from Super Bowl-winning former return ace and running back Brian Mitchell . The ex-Washington, Philadelphia Eagles and New York Giants great, who is the league's all-time leader in total return yards, vented his fury at how the Ravens have changed Henry's most-effective running style. Finlay could barely believe how new Ravens quarterback Jacoby Brissett had "49 pass attempts" on his debut against the Chargers. As Finlay put it, "Henry had 10 carries in a game they were never out of it." Ravens' $140 Million Star Called Out for Lack of ‘Leadership' After Loss Roquan Smith Calls Out Ravens Teammates After 6th Loss NFL Great Trashes Ravens for Making Derrick Henry Change Unlock the latest Heavy on Ravens news — direct to your inbox. There's something different about Derrick Henry in 2026, and one of the NFL's greatest all-time players blames the Baltimore Ravens for changing arguably the best running back of the modern era. Henry is enduring the roughest portion of his otherwise decorated career, and the frustration is starting to show. Tension boiled over when Henry snapped at reporters after gaining just 10 yards on as many carries during the 23-20 defeat to the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football. Mitchell told 106.7 The Fan co-host JP Finlay , "Derrick Henry is a locomotive. Why are you giving him the ball sliding in? He's supposed to catch it downhill to punish you. I don't get that. They're not utilizing him in the way he should be used." This is an interesting stylistic argument from Mitchell. He's drawn a parallel between how the Ravens used to run Henry and how first-year offensive coordinator Declan Doyle is using the two-time NFL rushing champion. It's an argument that puts the blame for Henry's alarming decline this season on the coaches. Unlike a Super Bowl winner for the Ravens, who believes 32-year-old Henry is waning physically . New Scheme's a Tough Fit for Derrick Henry Mitchell's speaking to Doyle shifting the Ravens away from the straight-ahead power they often favored under previous OCs, including Todd Monken and Greg Roman. This season's rushing attack is defined more by outside and lateral, stretch runs . It's a finesse-style of ground game, but Henry isn't completely unfamiliar with the concepts. He's long been an astute zone and cutback-type runner. home.blurb: Carolina Panthers safety Zakee Wheatley has received an NFL fine for the controversial hit that knocked Denver Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle out of their Week 9 matchup with a concussion. The play occurred with 19 seconds remaining in the first quarter of Carolina's 26-21 loss to Denver on November 8. Wheatley was not penalized for the hit during the game, despite Waddle subsequently entering concussion protocol and being ruled out. The officials did not penalize Wheatley. Instead, Panthers cornerback Marco Wilson drew flags for defensive pass interference and taunting on the same play. home.headline: Panthers are expected to get a key piece back on the field in Week 11 that can help change the dynamic of Carolina's offense
home.blurb: Dave Canales delivered good news Wednesday ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Ravens involving three players expected to return from injury, and the timing for one player matters for a backfield that has leaned heavily on one player all season. The Carolina Panthers are expecting more reinforcements going into Sunday's game against the Baltimore Ravens. Head coach Dave Canales told reporters Wednesday that running back Jonathon Brooks and cornerback Mike Jackson are both ready to return to action, and the same goes for offensive lineman Brady Christensen. Canales added it ultimately depends on roster management discussions with general manager Dan Morgan to see how the team can open up those three spots in order to bring all three players back. Still, it sounds like Carolina should have Brooks, Jackson, and Christensen back for the stretch run. All three players have been working their way back into football shape during their 21-day practice windows and will be key players to have back in the fold. And the conversation around Brooks' return is the most interesting one to have. The return I'm most focused on out of those three is Brooks. The Panthers had high hopes for him coming into this season, and 2026 was supposed to finally be his breakout year. Brooks had an injury-riddled first two years in the NFL and hardly got to play at all because of it. That's why his summer was so encouraging. Brooks put together a strong training camp and a strong preseason, flashing lightning-in-a-bottle speed throughout camp. It looked like he was finally going to be a real factor in this offense, and the Panthers were finally going to see a return on their investment in the former second-round pick. Brooks' return is a big advantage for Hubbard, because the Panthers have been working their lead back like a horse over the last couple of weeks. Hubbard currently ranks eighth in the NFL with 161 carries. Carolina has only run the ball 222 times as an offense, which means Hubbard has handled the overwhelming majority of the team's rushing attempts. "It goes beyond the game. It's also the week of work and making sure that the other guys are ready to go and making sure Chuba doesn't feel like he has to take all of the reps throughout the week," Canales explained. "He also has been responsible with that and understands what that load looks like." While the Panthers have been leaning heavily into him, Hubbard has still been conscious of his workload while still coming through in a big way. That was on full display Sunday against the New Orleans Saints . Hubbard put the team on his back with 172 total yards and two touchdowns. Now the Panthers have Brooks back, a player they had a strong vision for in a two-back offense. home.headline: Panthers injury report is full of reinforcements
home.blurb: The Carolina Panthers are flailing as they try to stay afloat at the top of the ever pitiful NFC South. The team has dropped three straight games with a skeleton crew of a secondary and a revolving door of players on the offensive line. The first injury report of Week 10 brings good news though. It looks like a lot of key players are soon to return. The highlight of this injury report is all of the full participation from guys that have been out for extended periods of time. Mike Jackson, Jonathon Brooks, and Xavier Legette all had their practice windows opened on Wednesday. That doesn't guarantee that they'll be active on Sunday, but it does mean they need to be activated within the next three weeks. And the fact that they all practiced in full would suggest they're all very close to getting back to live game action. The Saints are very banged up along their offensive line. Starting center Erik McCoy is out. Both starters to his left and the backup left tackle are all dealing with their own injuries, though it doesn't seem like any will miss the game this weekend. Running back Travis Etienne is back at practice, but I wouldn't be surprised if he misses the game even after a limited practice since teams tend to be very cautious with muscle injuries like that.
