The Jets are now 2-8 on the season. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-22 record and a 0-9 record in the AFC East. This is not good. This week the Jets were home to take on the Buffalo Bills. They kept it competitive for a little more than a half. At halftime the Jets trailed 10 – 6. The Jets got the ball to start the third quarter. Cade Klubnik took over for an injured Geno Smith and made a few nice plays with his leg and his arm to get the Jets in scoring position. They settled for a field goal to get within a point of the Bills at 10 – 9 early in the third quarter. That was as close as the Jets would get in the game. The Bills outscored the Jets 21 – 3 the rest of the way as Klubnik and the Jets offense were no match for Josh Allen and the Bills offense. The drubbing at the hands of the Bills left the Jets with a 2-8 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season's end. The Jets are also just one loss away from their 11th straight losing season. The last time the Jets won more than seven games in a season Barack Obama was still President. Now the Jets go on the road to face the only winless team left in the NFL, the Los Angeles Chargers. The Chargers play the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football, so it's possible they will no longer be winless by the time they face the Jets. The Chargers rank dead last in the NFL in points scored, with Justin Herbert somehow crashing to by far the lowest point in his career. After spending his entire career in the vicinity of a top 10 quarterback in the NFL, Herbert has arguably been the worst starting quarterback in the league this year. New Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniels' system appears to be a poor match for Herbert's skill set, and the result has been an offensive train wreck. The Chargers have not scored more than 23 points in any game this season, and they have not allowed less than 22 points in any game this season. It's tough to win games like that, but the Jets may prove to be an elixir for what ails the Chargers. Let's take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . The oddsmakers think the Chargers will beat the Jets next Sunday. It's come to this: the Jets aren't even favored over a winless team. The current line has the Jets road underdogs by 3.5 points. The game has an over/under of 40.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are +156 while the Chargers are -186. A loss next Sunday against the Chargers would be just another humiliation for the Jets. Perhaps they can find a way to avoid that fate after being beaten by a winless Dolphins team earlier this season. Perhaps. Perhaps not. Does it really matter in another lost Jets season? J-E-T-S! The New York Jets could turn to rookie Cade Klubnik for his first NFL start Sunday, with Geno Smith’s ankle injury leaving coach Aaron Glenn without a firm answer at quarterback. “We’ll see how the week goes,” Glenn said. The decision concerns Smith’s health, not an announced benching. Glenn said Monday that Smith would retain the job if healthy, The Associated Press reported . Tests did not reveal a serious ankle injury, but New York still needs to determine whether he can play. The Jets are 2-8 after five consecutive losses. They have not scored a touchdown in nine quarters, and a change at quarterback would put a fourth-round pick from Clemson in charge of an offense struggling to finish drives. Klubnik made his professional debut against Buffalo and completed 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards with an interception. He also ran three times for 26 yards. Glenn praised the rookie’s mobility Wednesday and said he would continue getting practice opportunities against the first- and second-team defenses. Klubnik had little time to settle in, but his first possession produced a 10-play, 61-yard drive and a field goal. Two scrambles moved the chains on that series, the team reported Monday . He played 37 snaps in relief of Smith. Running back Breece Hall came away encouraged by how Klubnik handled the huddle. Hall said the rookie showed more than he expected while stepping into a game without the preparation afforded a starter. “Just seeing how he came in, that was a huge growth step for him,” Hall said. home.headline: Geno Smith Injury Update, New NFL Rumors on Jets QB's Status Ahead of Chargers Game
home.blurb: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith will participate in Wednesday's practice in limited capacity after suffering multiple injuries in last Sunday's loss to the Buffalo Bills, head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters. The Jets (2-8) are on track for a high pick in the 2027 NFL draft. Should Smith remain available to start, the Jets may not get a longer look at Klubnik before deciding whether to use that pick on a quarterback. Smith left Sunday's game twice for a concussion evaluation and then for the ankle injury. He will be listed on the injury report with an ankle injury, Glenn said. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Monday Smith "underwent tests today that did not reveal anything major." "Smith, whose ankle provided the biggest concern, will continue to be evaluated through the week," Rapoport reported. The Jets are preparing to play Sunday at the Los Angeles Chargers. Glenn confirmed earlier this week Smith will continue starting over Cade Klubnik if healthy. When asked Wednesday if he expected Smith to play against the Chargers, Glenn said , "We'll see how the week goes." Smith left Sunday's game in a golf cart, then visited the X-rays before leaving without visible crutches or walking boot, per ESPN's Rich Cimini . ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Smith "was in pain Sunday but showed signs of improvement Monday, giving confidence that he will try to push through and play Sunday vs. Los Angeles." SNYs Connor Hughes reported the Jets shut down offers at the trade deadline for Smith, who has completed 67.1 percent of his passes with 2,226 passing yards to go along with 12 touchdowns and three interceptions in 10 games of his age-36 season. Klubnik saw his first action of the season when he went 11-for-20 with 137 yards after replacing Smith in Sunday's third quarter. home.headline: Jets’ Geno Smith gets injury update ahead of Chargers clash
home.blurb: As the Jets prepare for a critical Week 11 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers, aiming to end a painful five-game losing streak, all eyes are on Smith's practice availability. In an update from Florham Park, veteran ESPN beat reporter Rich Cimini provided clarity on Smith's participation: "QB Geno Smith (ankle) will be limited today, per Glenn." Smith's limited participation in practice is a positive sign, especially after he required X-rays at the stadium and was seen leaving MetLife Stadium on a golf cart following Sunday's defeat. Despite Smith's modest performance, completing 13 of 21 passes for 148 yards before his exit against Buffalo, head coach Aaron Glenn quickly dismissed any talk of a quarterback controversy between Smith and Klubnik. In a videoconference with reporters, Glenn firmly stated, "Geno's our starter. Come on now, let's not do that. I think Geno's had a really good year, and it would be disrespectful to him to just [replace him]." With Smith returning to practice, even in a limited capacity, the Jets are clearly counting on their established QB1 to lead the offense this Sunday. home.headline: Breaking Down Jets' Injury Outlook to Begin Week 11 (Who's Hurt & Who Could Return vs. Chargers)
home.blurb: Breaking Down Jets' Injury Outlook to Begin Week 11 (Who's Hurt & Who Could Return vs. Chargers) - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Because of the NFL's aggressive and physical nature, it's nearly impossible for a team to finish a game without a player suffering an injury. While injuries are part of the game, some teams sustain more injuries than others, which ultimately affects how their season plays out. Omar Cooper Jr. sustained an ankle injury on the first play and didn't return to the game. Dylan Parham and Geno Smith also suffered injuries and were unable to return. Even though Jarvis Brownlee Jr. was listed as a limited participant on Friday, he was ruled out against the Bills with an illness. The former Louisville Cardinal has had an up-and-down season, recording 11 total tackles and a sack across eight games. If Brownlee is either a full or limited participant in the Jets' upcoming practices, we should expect him to play against the Chargers. Since re-injuring his quad in Week 6 against the Patriots, Mauigoa has been on injured reserve, but he is eligible to return for Week 11's matchup with the Chargers. The Athletic's Zack Rosenblatt reported Friday that Mauigoa was one of seven players on injured reserve who were working out off to the side of practice . This doesn't mean Mauigoa will play next Sunday, but his appearance at practice indicates that he's ramping up and getting closer to making a return. Trevin Wallace was the only player who didn't participate in any of the Jets' practices last week and, as a result, was ruled out for Week 10's matchup due to a groin injury. Although the injury has sidelined him for the past two weeks, it hasn't had major consequences for New York's special teams. Even though Wallace hasn't impressed in this role, recording just three total tackles and earning a 63.9 special teams grade , per Pro Football Focus , the team could use all the contributors it can get after allowing a 95-yard kickoff return for a touchdown to Dylan Laube two weeks ago. If Wallace can be a full participant in any of the team's practices this week, we should anticipate his return to the lineup next Sunday. If Smith is available and practices during the week, we should expect the 14-year veteran to suit up. But if he doesn't, New York will turn to rookie Cade Klubnik as its starter.Although Klubnik showed some flashes, he needs more time and reps before he can be a reliable starter. Tyler Baron (knee), Anez Cooper (shoulder), Marcelino McCrary-Ball (ankle), Max Mitchell (head/concussion), David Onyemata (groin), and T'Vondre Sweat (ACL sprain) are all on the short-term injured reserve list and are eligible to return this season. They currently sit at 7-2, are in the hunt for the AFC West title and the top seed in the AFC. Even better is the week off should allow the Broncos to get players back from injury, especially on defense. All of this to say Denver is in a great spot. Now come the hated Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, led by rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza. The Broncos want to build on this great start to the season and carry the momentum over from the bye this Sunday against their rivals. Denver is a massive -10-point home favorite against the Raiders (4-6) at FanDuel Sportsbook. The total sits at over/under 40.5 points, with a lean toward the under at -115. Here are the MHR staff's keys to Sunday's game. Just win, baby! (By starting fast offensively) The best way to put pressure on a rookie quarterback is to make the Las Vegas offense one-dimensional. Bo Nix and the Broncos offense can do their part by starting Sunday's game fast offensively and finishing drives with touchdowns. We saw glimpses of this against the Carolina Panthers, with some deep shots early by Nix, but Denver had to kick a field goal on the opening drive. Replicate that this Sunday, but finish the opening drive with a touchdown. And then do it again. And then again. Add to the pressure that the Broncos defense will undoubtedly bring on the rookie QB. — Ian St. Clair Get after Fernando Mendoza Last week, Fernando Mendoza got his first career NFL start against a fierce Seattle Seahawks defense. Prior to Mendoza being a starter, the Raiders' offensive line only allowed 11 sacks when Kirk Cousins was quarterback. Last Sunday, with the 2026 NFL Draft's top pick under center, they gave up six to the Seahawks. If Denver wants to win the game, their defensive front seven has to dominate. Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph needs to throw everything he can at the rookie signal caller and rattle him early and often. — Christopher Hart Keep feeding Jonah Coleman I don't need to discuss numbers. Just look at how much better the offense is when Coleman gets his touches. Whether he's running the ball or catching passes, he gives the offense a weapon that forces the defense to respect what Denver is doing in the trenches, thus opening up the opportunities for Bo Nix to push the ball downfield. — Adam Malnati Blow a team out for once I know, I know. It's just not how this team is built. Every team gets a chance to beat the Broncos, but most of them fail to do so in the final minutes. Buuuuut, it would sure be nice to enjoy a good ol' fashioned butt-whoopin' type game — especially against the Raiders. — Tim Lynch Score more points than the Raiders The Broncos scored more points than the Panthers a few weeks ago and didn't need to score any last week, because they were on a bye. Now, it's Raiders week, and my key to the game is simple. Score more points than the Raiders. Denver is 7-0 when it does that and 0-2 when it does not. Using advanced analytics, I say the Broncos have a 100% chance to win on Sunday if they score more points than the Raiders. away.headline: Jaylen Waddle Full Participant at Broncos Practice After Concussion Before Raiders Game
away.blurb: He had company. Cornerback Riley Moss, who was also concussed against the Panthers, was a full participant, along with safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) for the first time since Week 5. Safety Brandon Jones (hamstring) and cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle) were limited, and every player on the active roster took part. “The guys that were or currently are injured are here,” Sean Payton said. “And it’s good to have everyone back.” Waddle has 52 targets, five more than Courtland Sutton , but his production has come in bursts. Pull out his Week 2 game against Jacksonville and the gap is plain: eight catches for 138 yards that day, and 22 catches for 199 yards across his other eight games. Entertainment Entertainment Home ··· Boxing Jaylen Waddle was back on the practice field Wednesday as the Denver Broncos returned from their bye, and their first injury report of Raiders week listed him as a full participant. Waddle hasn’t played since a first-quarter concussion at Carolina on Nov. 8. Will Jaylen Waddle play vs. Raiders? All signs point that way, though he isn’t officially cleared yet. The Denver Post’s Parker Gabriel noted Waddle and Moss were working through concussion protocol when they returned. A full practice is one of the last steps, and an independent neurological consultant still has to sign off before Sunday. Payton said there are “a handful of players that may not have been able to play” had the Broncos played last Sunday “that will have a chance of playing this Sunday.” Friday’s injury report, with game designations, will tell the rest. What Waddle gives Denver’s offense For an offense that converts 32% of its third downs , Denver needs more of the Jacksonville version, especially with Bo Nix’s passing game still searching for consistency. Ball security matters this week, too. Payton said the Raiders “force fumbles better than anyone in the league,” and Waddle’s last snaps at Carolina ended with the ball knocked loose. Getting Waddle back on offense and Moss back in a secondary Denver patched without three starters at Carolina would put the Broncos close to full strength for the first time since early October. away.headline: Raiders brace for bad news on star tight end ahead of Broncos showdown
away.blurb: Tight end Brock Bowers missed Wednesday’s practice with the ankle injury that knocked him out of the Raiders’ 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. Coach Klint Kubiak said Bowers was progressing but remained day-to-day. Bowers has not been ruled out against Denver. His absence Wednesday does, however, leave Las Vegas preparing for an AFC West road game without knowing how much its most productive pass catcher can contribute. Bowers injured his ankle while blocking early against Seattle. He returned briefly but was ruled out for the second half, as he finished with two catches for 18 yards. The Raiders offense declined sharply after its promising start. The Las Vegas Raiders opened preparations for Sunday’s game the Denver Broncos without their top target in practice. The Raiders are 4-6 after consecutive losses. Denver, 7-2 and tied for first in the AFC West, returns from its bye riding a five-game winning streak. Fernando Mendoza will make his second career start against a defense that ranks among the NFL ’s top 10 in sacks, pressures and quarterback hits. Bowers leads Las Vegas with 50 catches, 676 receiving yards and six touchdown receptions. Losing him would remove the offense’s leader in all three categories while Mendoza is still adjusting to starting in the NFL. Mendoza completed 11 of 13 passes for 90 yards before halftime and scored on a 10-yard run. Seattle eventually sacked him six times. After a second-quarter field goal, the Raiders punted on seven straight possessions and gained just 24 yards over that stretch. Kubiak acknowledged that losing Bowers affected the offense, but he put responsibility for finding other ways to move the ball on himself. “So I look at myself,” Kubiak said. “I have to do a much better job of moving the ball and spreading the ball around.” Denver presents another difficult assignment. Its defense has allowed 20.7 points per game, ninth in the league, and has recorded 26 sacks. The Raiders have averaged only 70.7 rushing yards per game, ranking 31st, so the ground game isn’t easing the pressure on a young quarterback. Wednesday’s update leaves Bowers’ availability unresolved. Las Vegas can get him back before Sunday’s 1:25 p.m. PT kickoff, but Mendoza and Kubiak cannot yet count on having their leading receiver against the Broncos. home.blurb: Caleb Lohner warms up. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The big news is Lohner's return from the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) List. The Broncos started his clock today, buying themselves a 21-day window to decide whether to activate him. The big news is Lohner's return from the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) List. The Broncos started his clock today, buying themselves a 21-day window to decide whether to activate him. If they don't activate Lohner, he'll be unavailable the rest of the season. If he is activated — and we should assume he will be — it'll be interesting to see how the Broncos juggle the roster math. At whose expense will Lohner's return be? Rookie tight end Dallen Bentley? Or it could be a player at another position. Meanwhile, all three players who suffered concussions in Carolina returned to practice in full, meaning they've cleared the protocol. Moss and Waddle are starters, so their return will be huge, while Prentice is a key role player who also contributes a lot on special teams. Abrams-Draine and Jones are a little more concerning, being limited, but it's too early to get worried. They've had two weeks to heal up, so we'll monitor Thursday and Friday's practice report, but it would be a surprise if they weren't cleared to play on Sunday. If Bowers is a no-go on Friday, he'll likely be ruled out of action. But if he's limited, there's a chance he could play. This game has been penciled in as a loss for the Giants for weeks now, and it shouldn't be much of a surprise to anyone paying attention that the 5-3-1 Giants are (nearly) touchdown underdogs to the 7-2 Jaguars. The Giants are coming off of a disappointing, and frustrating, loss to the Washington Commanders, squandering a golden opportunity to put the NFC East in a strangle hold and cement their position as a playoff contender. The Giants had multiple opportunities to put the game away, and instead played to not-lose on offense and defense — only to lose anyway. The Jaguars, meanwhile, are coming off of a 40-23 win over the Tennessee Titans, though that game was closer than the final score until the final 5 minutes or so. One of the biggest questions in the upcoming game is how the Jaguars will incorporate their newly acquired defensive players. The Jags elected to rest NT Jordan Davis and S Jesse Bates, both of whom were acquired in trades last week. DT Devon Godcheaux (acquired from the New Orleans Saints) did play, and ended the game with a tackle. The Giants can find comfort in the fact that they were 10.5-point underdogs on the road to the Houston Texans and came away with a win. However, the Jaguars have been far better than the Texans were when the Giants played them in Week 7. The Giants can win this game, but they'll certainly have their work cut out for them. picks.blurb: NFL Week 11 picks and predictions, straight-up and ATS: Jaguars blow past Giants, Vikings stay hot with Kirk Skip to main content NFL NFL Standings NFL Free Agency NFL News by Team More NFL News Our NFL Sites MLB Standings MLB Trades and Transactions MLB Free Agency Baseball Insiders MLB News by Team More MLB News Our MLB Sites Draft Tracker NBA Free Agency NBA Standings NBA News by Team More NBA News Our NBA Sites Anaheim Ducks Boston Bruins Buffalo Sabres Calgary Flames Carolina Hurricanes Chicago Blackhawks Colorado Avalanche Columbus Blue Jackets Detroit Red Wings Edmonton Oilers Florida Panthers Los Angeles Kings Minnesota Wild Montreal Canadiens Nashville Predators New Jersey Devils New York Islanders New York Rangers Ottawa Senators Philadelphia Flyers Pittsburgh Penguins San Jose Sharks Seattle Kraken St. Louis Blues Tampa Bay Lightning Toronto Maple Leafs Vancouver Canucks Vegas Golden Knights Washington Capitals Winnipeg Jets COLLEGE College Football Men's College Basketball Women's College Basketball Men's College Baseball ABOUT Contact FanSided Network Meet the Editorial Team Our Entertainment Sites I'm not going to lie to you, NFL Week 11 isn't exactly loaded with marquee matchups. Teams like the Chicago Bears , Buffalo Bills , Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos — you know, the contenders in this league right now — are all matched up with teams well out of the playoff race. Throw in the fact that six teams are on bye, and the schedule gets leaner. But we do have two big-time matchups with the Jacksonville Jaguars visiting the New York Giants and then a huge Sunday Night Football showdown in Mexico City with the Minnesota Vikings taking on the San Francisco 49ers for NFC supremacy. But regardless of the quality of matchup, we have every game covered in our NFL picks and predictions. We're coming off of two winning weeks in a row and are getting our mojo back. Surely a week in which there are numerous double-digit spreads with heavy and deserved favorites won't come back to haunt us. But here we go, once again delivering with NFL picks for Week 11 with predictions for every game straight-up and against the spread. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. Toughest NFL Week 11 prediction to make Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Minnesota Vikings (+3) vs. San Francisco 49ers – in Mexico City Minnesota Vikings (+3) vs. San Francisco 49ers – in Mexico City Point blank, these are two of the three best teams in the NFC right now. So you throw in the fact that this game is at a neutral site in primetime and it makes it even more difficult. Looking at these two teams, though, people are going to look at the 49ers and their high-powered offense and be intrigued by that. But the Vikings have proven that, under Brian Flores, they're capable of slowing down anyone. Heck, the Lions and Packers both found that out — even if the Detroit got the win thanks to Kyler Murray. But now Kirk Cousins is back in the fold for Minnesota and we've seen him already step in and raise the baseline of the Vikings offense substantially. Who knew getting Justin Jefferson the ball was the smart play? It's that end of the field that ended up being my deciding factor here, though. The fact that the Vikings offense has found this new level of competency complements the defense so incredibly well. Moreover, the 49ers defense, though talented, hasn't exactly been infallible of late. So in Mexico City, give me the Vikings staying hot and establishing a foothold in the NFC. Easiest NFL Week 11 pick on the board Chicago Bears wide receiver Luther Burden III, quarterback Caleb Williams | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears (-11.5) New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears (-11.5) This feels scarily too easy. Like, have oddsmakers watched the Saints recently? This defense is struggling mightily right now and the offense isn't exactly lighting the world on fire anymore either. To add to that, the Bears have been clinical more often than not this season (the last time out against the Buccaneers where Caleb Williams couldn't stop throwing picks, notwithstanding). Now we get Ben Johnson and this team coming out of a bye where they've had time to gameplan and get healthier. Yeah, that's all lining up pretty heavily toward Chicago for me, especially with this game being played in the Windy City. It's not that I think this game will end up being just a mauling on the Bears' part (though that's also not out of the question). The Saints should be able to score a bit. But it feels like Chicago will just have more consistent and perhaps unstopped success that will ultimately allow them to pull away handily. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6.5) at Detroit Lions Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6.5) at Detroit Lions Yes, I'm aware that Baker Mayfield's health is (once again) in question coming into this game. That's not me saying I have full faith in Jalon Daniels getting back into the offense, though he didn't play that poorly when he had to step in earlier in the season. What I think people are overlooking in this matchup is the fact that the Lions are coming off of the win in Munich and now have to travel back across the country and not get a bye week between games. That has happened for eight teams this season, traveling back from Europe and playing again in one week, and those teams are 2-5-1 straight-up, much less against the spread favored by more than a touchdowns. When you then factor in losing Aidan Hutchinson last week and what that could mean for Detroit's defense — which I wasn't exactly over the moon about to begin with — there's a path here for the Bucs to keep this close. I'll still take the Lions to win straight-up, mainly because I'm a coward and understand they are the substantially better team in this matchup. However, I do think the Buccaneers keep the game within a possession when we get to the end of it. Home / NFL About Pitch a Story Privacy Policy Legal Disclaimer Accessibility Statement

Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The New York Giants and Jacksonville Jaguars meet Sunday afternoon at MetLife Stadium in a matchup between two division leaders. New York enters at 5-3-1 and atop the NFC East, while Jacksonville is 7-2 and in first place in the AFC South. The Jaguars have won three straight and emerged as one of the league’s most complete teams, ranking fourth at 29.9 points per game while allowing only 16.0, second-best in the NFL. Trevor Lawrence has thrown for 2,284 yards and 21 touchdowns, while Parker Washington leads Jacksonville with 645 receiving yards. Led by J.J. McCarthy , the Giants have been more modest offensively averaging 22.6 points per game, but their defense ranks among the NFL’s best against the pass, allowing fewer than 200 yards per game. The Giants are trying to bounce back after a painful 24-21 home loss to the Washington Commanders last Thursday. New York twice took second-half leads and went in front 21-17 when McCarthy connected with Isaiah Likely for a 66-yard touchdown with 8:13 remaining, but Jayden Daniels answered with a 71-yard game-winning drive, capped by a 32-yard touchdown pass to Stefon Diggs with 57 seconds left. McCarthy completed 23 of 36 passes for 293 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Cam Skattebo ran 18 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns and Likely exploded for nine catches, 127 yards and a score. New York actually outgained Washington 399-340 but converted only four of 12 third downs and couldn’t protect the late lead. The Jaguars, meanwhile, are coming off one of their best offensive performances of the season, a 40-23 road victory over Tennessee. Lawrence completed 25 of 35 passes for 352 yards, three touchdowns and one interception, becoming the eighth-youngest quarterback in NFL history to reach 20,000 career passing yards. Washington was his biggest weapon, catching seven passes for a career-high 152 yards and a touchdown, while Bhayshul Tuten added 88 rushing yards and a late touchdown. Jacksonville piled up 459 yards, controlled the ball for more than 38 minutes and converted seven of 14 third downs as it scored at least 30 points for the fourth consecutive game. The Jacksonville offense and specifically the Jags’ passing game against New York’s pass defense is the central matchup Sunday. These franchises don’t have an extensive rivalry, but their meetings have tended to be competitive: Jacksonville holds a 4-3 lead in the all-time regular-season series, with the teams alternating victories in each of their past five meetings. Their most recent matchup came on October 23, 2022, when the Giants rallied for a 23-17 victory in Jacksonville. Over their three-game winning streak they’ve averaged 38.3 points per game. The Giants’ defense looks strong on paper — 4th in yards allowed (329.22 per game) and 2nd in passing yards allowed (207.67) — but there’s a real crack in it. New York ranks 20th in rushing yards allowed (121.56 per game), 26th in yards per carry allowed (4.48), 29th in tackle efficiency (89.55), and 29th in missed tackle rate (10.45%). home.headline: Giants' Cam Skattebo Reveals Backflip Celebration's Future After Aidan Hutchinson's Knee Injury
home.blurb: Cam Skattebo is retiring the backflip. The New York Giants' running back said he will no longer do his signature celebration after seeing Detroit Lions' pass-rusher Aidan Hutchinson tear his ACL during a sack celebration on Sunday. "It's hard to see," Skattebo told reporters Monday. "I'm saying yeah [no more backflips]. Mentally, I'm like, 'I'm not doing that.' That ain't going to happen to me." He did add that he might bring back the backflip "if we go to the playoffs or something," but acknowledged that Hutchinson "didn't think about [the risk] either, and it happened." That said, Skattebo said neither Schoen nor Harbaugh had talked with him about the celebratory move after the Hutchinson injury. Still, he isn't ruling out bringing back the backflips for a special occasion like the playoffs. Jones had been the return specialist for the Giants following the season-ending foot injury suffered by Braxton Berrios earlier in the year. He had recently struggled with ball security and production in that role. New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo, known for his penchant for celebratory backflips, is apparently ready to shelve the action after suffering a season-ending knee injury during a post-sack celebration by Detroit Lions pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson last week. Skattebo, per the New York Post , told reporters that it was hard to see Hutchinson get injured the way he did. “I’m saying yeah (no more backflips). Mentally, I’m like, ‘I’m not doing that.’ That ain’t going to happen to me.” Skattebo’s backflips have been a source of consternation for both general manager Joe Schoen and head coach John Harbaugh. In May, while still recovering from a broken ankle suffered in his rookie campaign, he did a backflip at the Brian Burns Celebrity Softball Game. Then in early July at a FanFest event in New York City, Skattebo did another backflip on a bouncy stage, only this time failing to stick the landing. That action prompted Schoen to openly admit he'd told the running back to rethink doing the backflips. I did that the past two weeks. After a good Week 9 picking games, I was solid again in Week 10. I went 9-5 against the spread and 8-6 straight up. I'll take it. Two weeks in a row. Wow. The records after 10 weeks are now 95-54-1 straight up and 68-79-3 ATS. Climbing out of a huge hole, ATS has me now visibly seeing the .500 mark. Let's hope the hot streak stays as we move towards Thanksgiving. There are a ton of big spreads this week, so watch out. The dogs might be barking. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Indianapolis Colts (+12.5) at Houston Texans Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime If the Texans are to have any chance of making the playoffs, they have to win this one. The Colts are pretty much done, but they beat Miami last week. Daniel Jones struggled in that one, but the Texans' defense has really struggled. Look for the Colts to hang around here, but the Texans will win it. Pick: Texans 30, Colts 27 Miami Dolphins (+16.5) at Buffalo Bills Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Miami is playing consecutive road games after losing at Indianapolis, while the Bills are home for the first time after two road games. The Bills are playing better on defense in recent weeks against some lower-level quarterbacks. They get another one here in backup Kyle McCord . The Bills will score, as Josh Allen always plays well against Miami, but Miami stays around. Pick: Bills 31, Dolphins 19 New Orleans Saints (+11.5) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a bye, while the Saints lost to the Panthers last week. Chicago is much improved on defense. With the Saints unable to run the ball, it will put a lot of pressure on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough . Caleb Williams will bounce back from his four-interception game last time out against Tampa Bay and will play well here. Bears take it. Pick: Bears 24, Saints 16 Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) The Cowboys are bad on defense, but the Titans haven't exactly lit it up on offense. Cam Ward has played better as of late. Even so, look for the Cowboys offense to have a big day throwing it against a Tennessee defense that struggles against the pass. Dak Prescott will put up big numbers. Pick: Cowboys 37, Titans 23 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+7) at Detroit Lions The issue here is whether Baker Mayfield will play for the Bucs. If not, they will have big problems. The Lions are back home after beating up the Patriots in Germany last week. The offense was dominant that day, but this Tampa Bay defense is playing well. That will keep them in the game, but the uncertainty at quarterback will be too much to overcome. Pick: Lions 22, Bucs 17 Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs (-16.5) Carson Beck makes his first road start for the Cardinals and this is as tough as any place in the league to do so. That will make for a tough day for this limited Arizona offense. Blowout. They actually showed some offensive life in that game. The Jets have defensive issues, which the Chargers can take advantage of here. Quarterback Geno Smith is banged up for the Jets, which could mean rookie Cade Klubnik makes his first NFL start. Look for the Chargers to take advantage if that is the case as they get to 2-8 behind another solid showing by the offense. I think the Jaguars get the better of it. Look for them to run it well with Bhayshul Tuten . This will be about the 49ers offense vs. Brian Flores' defense. I think Kyle Shanahan will get the best of it as the 49ers keep rolling. Big day for Christian McCaffrey running it. The Bengals keep rolling. Our friends at the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the betting lines for this week, and the Vikings have started as a three-point underdog to the Niners. The over/under for this one has started at 46.5 points. The Vikings snapped their two-game losing streak this past Sunday at Lambeau Field, pasting the Green Bay Packers by a score of 30-10 to complete a sweep of the Border Battle for the 2026 season. The defense was dominant, sacking Jordan Love eight times and forcing three of the four turnovers committed by the Packers (the fourth came on special teams). But the big story was the Vikings' offense and the return of Kirk Cousins, whom the Vikings acquired at the trade deadline on Tuesday, arrived in Minnesota on Wednesday, and started on Sunday, making him the first player since at least 1950 to start games at quarterback for different teams in consecutive weeks. Cousins' last start for his former team, the Las Vegas Raiders, came against these same 49ers, who come into this game tied for the league's best record at 8-1. Like the Vikings, the Niners got their season off to a 6-0 start before seeing their first loss, a 29-20 defeat to the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7. After the bye, they came back to beat Cousins and the Raiders by a score of 38-17, and this past Sunday they had a back-and-forth battle with the Dallas Cowboys that saw them eventually emerge with a 46-40 victory at Jerryworld. Brock Purdy is on the short list of potential MVP candidates for this season, and he showed why against the Cowboys, completing 22-of-28 passes for 389 yards and three touchdowns, two of which came on long passes to Christian McCaffrey, who had 161 receiving yards on the day. This matchup looks to be another matchup of a very strong offense facing off against Brian Flores' #1 defensive squad. Unlike what we saw when the Vikings faced the Bills on Monday Night, however, now it appears that the Vikings have the offense to actually allow their defense to have a bit of a rest and not allow them to get worn down late in the game. For the fourth consecutive week, the Vikings will go into a game as an underdog, ladies and gentlemen. What do you think about that? Let us know in the comments!

picks.blurb: Vikings vs. 49ers bold predictions for Week 11 Sunday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Giannis red hot vs. Bucks Boone's trade charts Cowboys DC latest Vikings vs. 49ers bold predictions for Week 11 Sunday Night Football Ben Strauss, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Wed, November 18, 2026 at 10:17 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The playoff picture in the NFL is finally starting to come into focus ahead of Week 11. This week's Sunday Night Football matchup features two teams who each in the thick of the NFC playoff race. San Francisco is one of the league's best teams , sitting atop the standings with Buffalo at 8-1 on the season. Minnesota is one game back at 7-2 and fighting for their lives in a wildly competitive NFC North division race. NFL fans will be thrilled at the opportunity to watch San Francisco's offense go up against Minnesota's defense. That marquee matchup alone is the reason why this game has the potential to become an instant classic. But make no mistake, both of these teams are complete in all three phases and have excellent coaching. Something's got to give, and it will be exciting to see which unit takes over this contest. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) So who will come out on top in this one? And is the winner of this high-leverage game destined to make the postseason? Here are three bold predictions ahead of this epic Sunday Night Football showdown between the Vikings and 49ers. Brock Purdy does nothing but throw touchdowns, get sacked against elite Vikings defense Jerome Miron-Imagn Images The 49ers are getting plenty of praise this season and rightfully so. But Purdy deserves an even larger slice of that pie than he's currently getting. Purdy is quietly having the best season of his career. He is on pace to surpass his incredible 2023 season in almost every category. If Purdy stays on the same pace, he'll have more passing yards, more touchdowns, and fewer interceptions. Even when zooming out at the whole team, San Francisco went 12-5 in 2023. The 49ers are well ahead of schedule and should finish with a better record this season. Purdy's high level of play has made the difference. So how will he fare against arguably the best NFL defense of the past decade? Purdy will throw at least three touchdown passes against the vaunted Vikings defense. But Purdy won't get away so easy, as Minnesota will extract their pound of flesh too. The Vikings will log at least six sacks throughout this game. Just how bold is this prediction? Purdy has thrown three or more touchdowns three times this season. Meanwhile, the Vikings have put up six or more sacks twice in 2026. Minnesota even had eight sacks last week against Green Bay! The most important part of this prediction is the ratio. Purdy's number of touchdown passes must be exactly half compared to how many times he is sacked. While there is an initial line set, the prediction still holds regardless of how many sacks Purdy takes. Fans for both teams can enjoy tracking the status of this prediction throughout the night. Justin Jefferson has his best game since 2024 against the 49ers What if the legendary Justin Jefferson makes his triumphant return in Week 11? It's not too crazy of a thought with Kirk Cousins throwing him the ball again. Jefferson immediately improved once the Vikings got a capable quarterback under center. Of course, it does help that the pair have a strong relationship after years of playing together. The real question will be whether or not that chemistry can overcome their opponents solid defense. San Francisco's defense is middle of the road in terms of pass coverage. They've allowed 225.7 passing yards per game along with 16 receiving touchdowns in just nine games. The 49ers still have a great defense, but the numbers show that they are far from invincible. Let's assume the real Jefferson does return in Week 11, bringing levels of production not seen since the magical 2024 season. Minnesota's star receiver will log at least 125 receiving yards and at least one touchdown. The last time Jefferson was this productive was Week 16 of the 2024 season against the Seahawks. In that game, Jefferson hauled in 10 receptions for 144 receiving yards and two touchdowns. It's time for that Jefferson to return and guide the Vikings back to the playoffs. 49ers win an overtime thriller against the Vikings Kirby Lee-Imagn Images It will be fascinating to see how each team game plans against the other. Will Minnesota continue to blitz at an absolutely absurd rate against an offensive genius like Kyle Shanahan? And what will San Francisco's plan be for slowing down Kirk Cousins and Minnesota's offense? This game has the potential to turn into either a shootout or a defensive slugfest depending on some of those variables. That level of variability is what makes football so fun to watch. It's tempting to predict a tie in such a tight matchup like this. But both teams have so much to play for that somebody is bound to leave the stadium with a win. The Vikings will do everything they can to force overtime. While they will succeed, the 49ers will come out on top thanks to their superior firepower and coaching advantage. San Francisco prevails on a game-winning field goal. home.headline: 'Bush-league' — Mike Florio accuses 49ers of potentially keeping Brandon Aiyuk away from NFL rivals out of spite
home.blurb: Aiyuk was reinstated by the NFL after spending time on the reserve/left squad list, but the 49ers have yet to release him or add him to their 53-man roster. Florio pointed out that the team has continued to hold onto Aiyuk despite his reinstatement from the reserve/left squad list. “Nine days since Aiyuk was reinstated from the reserve/left squad list, the 49ers haven’t cut him. At this point, with only six days to go, the 49ers surely will kick the can as long as they can. They gain nothing from delaying Aiyuk’s return, other than the relatively minor strategic advantage of keeping him away from a competitor,” Florio said. Florio called out the 49ers for potentially holding Aiyuk back out of spite , describing such a move as “bush-league” and one that would create “bad karma.” He believes the 49ers should let the receiver return to the NFL rather than prolong the situation. “If the 49ers are simply squatting on Aiyuk out of spite, that’s a bush-league move that creates bad karma. Let the guy get back in the league,” Florio said. home.headline: Wednesday injury report: Vikings set to get a few key players back vs. 49ers
home.blurb: TE T.J. Hockenson (wrist) also has a shot to go. He was listed as limited in Wednesday's practice. WR Jordan Addison (thumb) and QB Kyler Murray (hamstring) were the only DNPs for Minnesota. It sounds like Addison could avoid an IR stint after undergoing a procedure on his thumb, but he's still going to miss at least a game or two. "I do anticipate Blake Cashman fully clearing the (concussion) protocol very soon and likely being available this Sunday," head coach Kevin O'Connell said on Wednesday. With no Addison, Jennings could be in line to serve as the Vikings' No. 2 receiver in a game against his former team this week. He's had a quiet season so far, but this could be an opportunity for a breakout performance, especially with Kirk Cousins at quarterback. Hockenson's return would also be big, although Gavin Bartholomew filled in nicely last week. "I think it's gonna be a boost to get Jauan back on the grass and hopefully have him available this week," O'Connell said. "He's a guy that can do a lot of things in our offense, and I think he's a guy that can make plays. We know he's gonna be competing this week, considering the opponent." Four other players were listed as limited for the Vikings: OLBs Andrew Van Ginkel (quad) and Kyle Van Noy (calf), S Jay Ward (knee), and WR Jeshaun Jones (shoulder). Van Ginkel is a big one to watch. He left the game in Green Bay in the second half and did not return. The early indications seem somewhat promising, but soft tissue injuries can be tough to predict. Van Ginkel is playing at an All-Pro level this season. "He got looked at a little bit for a lower leg, soft tissue type thing, but he's actually feeling pretty good," O'Connell said of Van Ginkel on Monday. "Expecting him to be able to work through the week, but more than likely be limited early on, and we're hoping to have him. I didn't ask him this, but if that would have been a game that we needed to continue to keep all our guys out there, I imagine he would have stayed in the football game."
